title: Quarterly Orbit Plan: Hosted API + Model Catalog Transition Playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: This playbook defines the quarterly execution plan ("Orbit Plan") for synchronizing Hosted API route rollouts with model-catalog transitions. The goal is to deliver predictable model lineups, clear canary windows, and contingency lanes for customer-facing endpoints while minimizing token-cost regressions and latency SLO violations. The plan covers scope selection, guardrails for model swaps, staffing/schedule alignment, and a lightweight ops-runbook for rapid rollback and postmortem capture.
acceptance_criteria: Model lineup for Tier-1 hosted routes is finalized and approved by PM + Applied ML
Canary gating checklist implemented in console for at least two routes
Runbook documented with rollback steps and playbook links in Confluence
Cost delta analysis completed showing <=10% expected unit-cost change for affected routes
Automated smoke/eval tests pass against canary traffic with baseline quality thresholds
milestones: M2: Canary windows scheduled and ops-runbook published - 2026-03-10
M4: Evaluate canary metrics and expand to 50% - 2026-03-24
risks: Latency SLO regressions if quantized variant selected for throughput without enough kernel testing
Unexpected token-cost increases for high-throughput routes due to batching mismatch
Model quality regressions on edge prompt sets not covered by standard evals
Staffing overlap risk during week-of release (on-call + PM rotation)
Interdependent infra changes (ENG-2207) could delay rollout windows
comments: 2026-02-25 Maya Patel: Created initial playbook. Main ask is to coordinate with Applied ML for final lineup recommendations.
2026-02-28 Liam O'Connor: Added preliminary milestone dates; requested ENG owners for canary automation (ENG-2207).
2026-03-02 Ana Gutiérrez (Applied ML): Flagging a potential quality delta on long-form summarization for model v2-ql; recommend expanding eval set by 20 prompts.
2026-03-04 Engineering review (ENG owners): Confirmed kernel compatibility for quantized variants on RTX-a100 clusters; noted a perf variance in 6k-token sequences.
2026-03-07 Design review (J. Kim): Console UX for canary gating looks good; asked for one additional confirmation modal for route owners before 10% rollout.
2026-03-09 Security: quick scan completed, no PII flow changes; KMS rotation schedule does not intersect release window.
decision_log: 2026-03-03 Decision: Freeze lineup to include gen-2-small (default) + gen-2-quant (fallback). Rationale: balance cost and latency; quant for low-priority routes.

2026-03-05 Decision: Canary window will use progressive traffic (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on any of the following: latency p95 > SLO by 30%, cost-per-token > 20% above baseline, or eval quality drop > 3 points.
2026-03-06 Tradeoff: Postpone multi-region expansion to Q2 to reduce cross-region rollback complexity; proceed with single-region canaries for Q1.
next_steps: Assign ENG owners for canary automation tasks (ENG-2207) - due 2026-03-05
Applied ML to deliver expanded eval set and a regression baseline - due 2026-03-08
Create a lightweight status dashboard for PM/ENG on canary metrics - due 2026-03-09
Schedule ops tabletop on rollback playbook and runbook rehearsals - due 2026-03-12
Confirm staffing overlap windows and on-call coverage for rollout week - due 2026-03-14
notes: Stakeholder alignment: Growth wants minimal churn for conversational endpoints; Platform wants to maximize model consolidation to reduce fleet overhead. The playbook includes two contingency lanes: (A) model-variant fallback (gen-2-small -> gen-1-stable) and (B) regional traffic shift to unaffected zone. Both lanes require pre-approved infra tickets and an on-call communications template.
postmortem_template: Postmortem outline: timeline, trigger, impact (requests & tokens), root cause, mitigation, action items, owner, due dates. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Release+Postmortem+Template
communication_plan: Pre-release: Stakeholder digest + runbook summary (48h before) to #release-updates on Slack and email to Customer Success
During canary: Hourly automated canary status posts to #canary-monitor; escalation channel includes ENG-Lead, PM, Applied ML
Post-release: 72h stability report and retrospective invite to cross-functional partners
